policy:
---

In the project section of the config dialog, we can select a background shade color for the application. It seems that this color is only applied after restarting the app or re-opening the project again.

This should be done when the config is saved.

So don't use a global project-wide event monitor for this, but use something specific, so the background only reloads when the config has changed

design\STYLE_GUIDE.md:17:- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` — MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
design\STYLE_GUIDE.md:82:- **On dark backgrounds shadows read as nothing** — the theme already handles this by making hover raise `borderColor` (`custom.borderHover`) instead of relying on shadow.
design\STYLE_GUIDE.md:102:- **Ghost icon button** (`IconButton`): transparent → hover `bgcolor: track` (or `background.paper` on a colored panel) + `color: primary.main`. Override MUI's default circular hover tint via `sx`.

entries.content:
The background shade is saved correctly, but the theme is not notified.

- [theme_provider.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/theme/theme_provider.tsx:24) reads the shade through `useProjectConfig()`.
- [use_project_config.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/hooks/use_project_config.ts:31) subscribes to the project-wide `DataService` event.
- Saving the dialog updates `ConfigService` through `saveDraft()` and emits only its config event ([config_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/config/config_service.ts:616)).
- The expected file-watcher event does not reload locally saved config. Consequently, the theme updates only after another `DataService` event or reopening the project.

Proposed solution: read `project.backgroundShade` in `AppThemeProvider` through the existing `useConfigValueOrFallback` hook. Its primitive snapshot causes React to rebuild the theme only when that specific canonical value changes, not for unrelated project updates or draft edits.

Add a test proving that saving a changed shade updates the theme immediately, while merely editing the draft does not. No files were changed.
